cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code demonstrates explicit bounds checking before array access. Line 307 validates that an index (txn.inputs[i].outputIndex) is within the bounds of input_slpmsg.sendOutputs array before accessing it on line 308.

connection.evidence: External transaction data flows through txn.inputs[i].outputIndex from blockchain transactions via retrieveRawTransaction method. This attacker-controlled index is directly used in the bounds check and subsequent array access at line 308.

diff_causality.evidence: The added bounds check prevents out-of-bounds array access that would occur without this validation. Reverting this line would remove the protection, allowing invalid indices to access memory outside the sendOutputs array bounds.

security_control.evidence: The bounds check is the required security control for preventing buffer overread. It validates the index against the actual array length before access.
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-119 requires proper bounds checking to prevent accessing memory outside allocated buffer boundaries
existing_controls_checked: No other bounds validation exists for this specific array access path in the code context
security_control.deficiency_evidence: Without this check, the code would directly access array elements using unvalidated external input

concrete_impact.evidence: Out-of-bounds access to sendOutputs array could lead to reading invalid token quantities, potentially causing incorrect token validation decisions or application crashes.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the code would directly access input_slpmsg.sendOutputs array at line 308 using an unvalidated index, potentially reading outside the array bounds and causing memory access violations or incorrect token calculations.
supporting_evidence: Line 308: Array access 'input_slpmsg.sendOutputs![txn.inputs[i].outputIndex!]' demonstrates the vulnerable operation
External transaction data flows to txn.inputs[i].outputIndex via retrieveRawTransaction method
unresolved_facts: Whether the retrieveRawTransaction method properly sanitizes all transaction input data
Potential error handling for malformed transaction indices in other code paths
review_comment: The added bounds check properly validates transaction input indices against SLP output array lengths before accessing token quantities. This prevents out-of-bounds memory access that could occur when processing maliciously crafted blockchain transactions. Ensure all similar array access patterns in the SLP validation logic receive equivalent bounds validation to maintain consistent security.
